{{Short description|American mathematician (1906–1971)}}
[[File:ArchieBlakeSignature.jpg|thumb|Signature of Archie Blake]]
Charles Archibald Blake (November 24, 1906 - January 7, 1971), name officially changed to '''Archie Blake''' <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seekingmyroots.com/members/files/G000068.pdf|title=Some of the Archibald Tribe}}</ref> was an American mathematician.
He is well known for the [[Blake canonical form]], a [[normal form (mathematics)|normal form]] for [[expression (mathematics)|expressions]] in [[propositional logic]].
In order to compute the canonical form, he moreover introduced the concept of [[consensus theorem|consensus]], which was a precursor of the [[resolution (logic)|resolution]] principle, today a common technique in [[automated theorem proving]].

==Career==
In 1930, he became a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS).<ref>''[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|Bulletin of the AMS]]'', [https://www.ams.org/bull/1931-37-03/S0002-9904-1931-05095-3/S0002-9904-1931-05095-3.pdf Mar 1931], Vol.37, No.3,  p.3(131), "Annual meeting in Cleveland, Dec 29-31, 1930"</ref><ref>''Bulletin of the AMS'', Oct 1931, Vol.37, No.9, [https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1931-37-09/S0002-9904-1931-05239-3/S0002-9904-1931-05239-3.pdf "Additional members of the Society and changes of title or address October, 1931"]. Blake is designate as new member.</ref> He presented his canonical form at the AMS meeting at [[Columbia University]] on 29 Oct 1932.<ref>''[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|Bulletin of the AMS]]'', [https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1933-39-01/S0002-9904-1933-05527-1/S0002-9904-1933-05527-1.pdf Jan 1933], Vol.39, No.1, p.1,2</ref>
In 1937, this work lead to a [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Chicago]], supervised by Raymond Walter Barnard.<ref>{{mathGenealogy|6342}}</ref>

He worked for the [[United States Coast and Geodetic Survey]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], from 1936 (or earlier) as a [[mathematician]],<ref>[http://www.ams.org/bull/1936-42-09/S0002-9904-1936-06389-5/S0002-9904-1936-06389-5.pdf AMS Member List], Sep 1936, p.4(16)</ref> since 1938 as an Assistant Mathematician,<ref>[https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1938-44-09/S0002-9904-1938-06837-1/S0002-9904-1938-06837-1.pdf AMS Member List], Sep 1938, p.4(14)</ref> and since 1939 as an Associated Mathematician.<ref>The University of Chicago Magazine [https://campub.lib.uchicago.edu/text/?docId=mvol-0002-0031-0006 Mar 1939]: ''"Archie Blake, SM'31, PhD'37, has recently been appointed associate mathematician for the U S. Coast and Geodetic Survey, in Philadelphia."''</ref><ref>[http://www.ams.org/bull/1940-46-09/S0002-9904-1940-07303-3/S0002-9904-1940-07303-3.pdf AMS Member List], Sep 1940, p.4(12)</ref>
In 1946, he was appointed a Senior Statistician in the Office of the [[Army Surgeon General]], [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>''Bulletin of the AMS'', [https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1946-52-09/S0002-9904-1946-08651-6/S0002-9904-1946-08651-6.pdf Sep 1946], Vol.52, No.9, p.2(801)</ref>
He also worked for the [[Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory]] in [[Buffalo, New York]].
From there, he changed in 1954 to the [[Westinghouse Electric Corporation]] in [[Baltimore, Md.]], where he became an Advisory Engineer.<ref>[[AMS Notices]], [https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/195410/195410FullIssue.pdf Issue No.5], Oct 1954, p.12</ref>
In 1956, he moved from Westinghouse to the [[Bendix Aviation Corporation]], as a Systems Staff Mathematician.<ref>[[AMS Notices]], [https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/195608/195608FullIssue.pdf Issue No.18], Aug 1956, p.41</ref>
In 1960, he became a Manager of the Analysis Section of [[Raytheon]] in [[Sudbury, Massachusetts]].<ref>[[AMS Notices]], Vol.7, No.3, [https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/196006/196006FullIssue.pdf Issue 46], Jun 1960, p.45(321)</ref>
